He played four years of college basketball for [[Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets men's basketball|Georgia Tech]] before having stints in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA) with the [[Chicago Bulls]] in 2006 and the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] in 2007. In 2010, he won an [[List of NBL champions|NBL championship]] with the [[Perth Wildcats]]. ==Early life and career== Schenscher was born in the small [[South Australia]]n suburb of Hope Forest, just east of the town of [[Willunga, South Australia|Willunga]] where he grew up on a five-acre farm.{{cite web|last=Drehs|first=Wayne|url=http://www.espn.com.au/mens-college-basketball/ncaatourney04/columns/story?id=1775517|title=Schenscher's impact grows with each game|work=ESPN.com|date=5 April 2004|accessdate=20 February 2019}} As a junior, he played basketball for the [[Noarlunga City Tigers]].{{cite web|url=http://www.southerntigers.com.au/history|title=Our Club's History|work=southerntigers.com.au|accessdate=20 February 2019}} In 1999, he moved to [[Canberra]] to attend the [[Australian Institute of Sport]] in conjunction with [[UC Senior Secondary College Lake Ginninderra|Lake Ginninderra College]].{{cite web|url=https://ramblinwreck.com/seven-foot-australian-luke-schenscher-enrolls-at-tech-joins-basketball-team/|title=SEVEN-FOOT AUSTRALIAN LUKE SCHENSCHER ENROLLS AT TECH, JOINS BASKETBALL TEAM|work=ramblinwreck.com|date=23 August 2001|accessdate=20 February 2019}} Between 1999 and 2001, he played for the [[BA Centre of Excellence|AIS men's team]] in the [[South East Australian Basketball League]].{{cite web|url=http://www.ausport.gov.au/ais/sports/basketball/athletes/past_athletes|title=Past Athletes|work=ausport.gov.au|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20140212073754/http://www.ausport.gov.au/ais/sports/basketball/athletes/past_athletes|archivedate=12 February 2014}} In 2001, he led the team in scoring (15.2 points per game) and rebounding (9.2 per game), while also averaging 1.65 blocks per game and shooting 54 percent from the floor. He was subsequently named AIS Junior Athlete of the Year.{{cite web|url=https://www.abc.net.au/news/2005-08-19/luke-schenscher-makes-it-two-australians-in-the-nba/2084834|title=Luke Schenscher makes it two Australians in the NBA|work=abc.net.au|date=19 August 2005|accessdate=20 February 2019}} Also in 2001, he became the first high school student to play for the [[Australia men's national basketball team|Boomers]] when he took part in the [[2001 East Asian Games|East Asian Games]]. Additionally, he was a member of the Australian national under-21 team which finished eighth at the [[FIBA Under-21 World Championship]]. ==College career== From 2001 to 2005, Schenscher played college basketball for [[Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets men's basketball|Georgia Tech]]. As a freshman, he started five of first six games before being sidelined for 12 games with a broken foot. He led Tech in field goal percentage (.587) and averaged 4.8 points and 3.2 rebounds for the season. As a sophomore, he started 16 games and ranked third on the team in field goal percentage (.472) and second in blocked shots (25).{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/draft2005/profiles/LukeSchenscher.html|title=Prospect Profile: Luke Schenscher|work=NBA.com|accessdate=20 February 2019}} As a junior in 2003–04, Schenscher finished fourth in the [[Atlantic Coast Conference|ACC]] in blocks (1.4 bpg) and eighth in rebounds (6.6 rpg). He shot .565 from the floor. He was the team's second leading scorer in the [[2004 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]], averaging 10.8 points along with 7.0 rebounds and 1.0 blocks. He helped the Yellow Jackets reach the NCAA Final Four, where he recorded 19 points and 12 rebounds in the semifinal win over [[Oklahoma State Cowboys basketball|Oklahoma State]], and nine points and 11 rebounds in the [[2004 NCAA Division I Men's Basketball Championship Game|final]] against [[Connecticut Huskies men's basketball|UConn]], a game the Yellow Jackets lost 82–73. As a senior in 2004–05, Schenscher averaged a career-best 10.1 points per game, to go with 7.3 rebounds and 1.75 blocks. He led the Yellow Jackets in field goal percentage (.539) but did not meet the minimum attempts to qualify for league leaders. In 119 games at Georgia Tech, Schenscher averaged 7.3 points, 5.4 rebounds and 1.32 blocks per game.{{cite web|url=http://www.insidehoops.com/schenscher-bulls-030506.shtml|title=Bulls sign Luke Schenscher to 10-day contract|work=InsideHoops.com|date=5 March 2006|accessdate=20 February 2019}} ==Professional career== ===NBA and D-League=== After going undrafted in the [[2005 NBA draft]], Schenscher joined the [[Denver Nuggets]]' Summer League team. He later signed with the Nuggets on 15 August before being waived on 3 October. He was claimed off waivers by the [[Sacramento Kings]] two days later, before they too waived him on 26 October.{{cite web|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/nba/transactions/league/2006|title=2005-2006 NBA Transactions|work=RealGM.com|accessdate=20 February 2019}} He subsequently joined the [[Fort Worth Flyers]] of the [[NBA Development League]], where he averaged 8.2 points, 6.1 rebounds, 1.42 blocks and 1.2 assists in 36 appearances with 34 starts during the 2005–06 season. He shot .530 from the floor and .607 from the free throw line. On 5 March 2006, Schenscher signed a 10-day contract with the [[Chicago Bulls]]. He went on to sign a second 10-day contract on 15 March, and a rest-of-season contract on 25 March.{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/bulls/news/schenscher_060304.html|title=Bulls Sign Schenscher for Remainder of Season|work=NBA.com|date=25 March 2006|accessdate=20 February 2019}} In 20 games for the Bulls, he averaged 1.8 points and 1.5 rebounds in 7.5 minutes per game.{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/s/schenlu01.html|title=Luke Schenscher Stats|work=Basketball-Reference.com|accessdate=20 February 2019}} After playing for the Bulls during Summer League and preseason, he was waived on 30 October 2006.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/bulls/news/schenscher_waived_061030.html|title=Bulls Waive Luke Schenscher|work=NBA.com|date=30 October 2006|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20080209235328/http://www.nba.com/bulls/news/schenscher_waived_061030.html|archivedate=9 February 2008}} He returned to the Flyers for the 2006–07 D-League season.{{cite news |title=Schenscher focused on flyers |url=http://www.basketballwa.asn.au/fs_newsitem.asp?id=68263&orgID=1&Oname=BA&O1c=8&O10c=3 |access-date=6 November 2025 he signed a 10-day contract with the [[Portland Trail Blazers]]. He went on to sign a second 10-day contract on 25 March, and a rest-of-season contract on 4 April.{{cite news |last1=Hawes |first1=Ben |title=Schenscher signed for remainder of NBA season |url=http://www.basketballwa.asn.au/fs_newsitem.asp?id=70068&orgID=1&Oname=BA&O1c=8&O10c=3 |access-date=6 November 2025 |work=basketballwa.asn.au |date=4 April 2007 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070902091349/http://www.basketballwa.asn.au/fs_newsitem.asp?id=70068&orgID=1&Oname=BA&O1c=8&O10c=3 |archive-date=2 September 2007}} In 11 games for the Trail Blazers, he averaged 1.7 points and 2.3 rebounds in 10.7 minutes per game. In July 2007, Schenscher played for the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]]' Summer League team.{{cite web|url=https://australia.basketball/schenscher-joins-boomers-camp/|title=SCHENSCHER JOINS BOOMERS CAMP|work=australia.basketball|date=18 July 2007|accessdate=20 February 2019}} ===Germany=== On 27 July 2007, Schenscher signed a one-year deal with German team [[Brose Baskets]].{{cite web|url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/14671/180/item|title=Brose Baskets signs Aussie center Luke Schenscher|work=Euroleague.net|date=27 July 2007|url-status=live|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20070930023726/http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/14671/180/item|archivedate=30 September 2007}} It was reportedly the highest fee ever paid by the club at the time.{{cite web|url=https://www.khgroup.com.au/schenscher-mind/|title=How the mind helps and hinders high performance|work=khgroup.com.au|date=7 October 2018|accessdate=20 February 2019}} He found the pressure of the big contract and the expectation that came with being an NBA player overwhelming, with the pressure translating to injuries on the court. He played only one game before returning to Australia to have surgery on his knee. ===NBL=== ====Adelaide 36ers==== In April 2008, Schenscher signed with the [[Adelaide 36ers]] for [[2008–09 NBL season]].{{cite web|last=Nagy|first=Boti|url=https://www.foxsports.com.au/basketball/sixers-land-schenscher/news-story/94fc3675f3b2a9072be75ddfde0a8a82|title=Sixers land Schenscher|work=FoxSports.com.au|date=14 April 2008|accessdate=20 February 2019}}{{cite web|url=https://www.abc.net.au/news/2008-04-15/schenscher-signs-with-sixers/2403542|title=Schenscher signs with Sixers|work=ABC.net.au|date=15 April 2008|accessdate=20 February 2019}} On 25 October 2008, he recorded 33 points and 20 rebounds against the [[Perth Wildcats]].{{cite web|url=http://websites.sportstg.com/team_info.cgi?action=PSTATS&pID=190396069&client=0-189-88237-232872-17885838&ocompID=125710|title=Player statistics for Luke Schenscher – 2008/09|work=SportsTG.com|accessdate=20 February 2019}} On 6 December 2008, he recorded 17 points and 22 rebounds against the [[Melbourne Tigers]]. On 13 February 2009, he recorded 37 points and 15 rebounds against the [[Wollongong Hawks]]. In 31 games, he averaged 16.9 points, 10.8 rebounds, 1.5 assists and 1.4 blocks per game. He subsequently earned [[All-NBL Team|All-NBL Second Team]] honours. The 36ers allowed Schenscher to part ways with them in the off-season in order to play with the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] in the NBA Summer League, but he aborted those plans due to a back injury.{{cite In April 2010, the Wildcats parted ways with Schenscher due to his wage demands being too high for the club to meet.{{cite web|last=Hope|first=Shayne|url=https://thewest.com.au/sport/basketball/schenscher-set-to-leave-wildcats-ng-ya-216197|title=Schenscher set to leave Wildcats|work=TheWest.com.au|date=11 April 2010|accessdate=20 February 2019}} ====Townsville Crocodiles==== Weeks after parting ways with the Wildcats, Schenscher signed with the [[Townsville Crocodiles]].{{cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cgJ6lP0emu4 |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/varchive/youtube/20211221/cgJ6lP0emu4 |archive-date=2021-12-21 |url-status=live|title=Crocs sign Luke Schenscher|work=[[YouTube]]|publisher=[[Townsville Crocodiles]]|date=27 April 2010|accessdate=20 February 2019}}{{cbignore}} On 30 October 2010, he recorded 26 points and 10 rebounds against the [[Sydney Kings]].{{cite web|url=http://websites.sportstg.com/team_info.cgi?action=PSTATS&pID=190396069&client=0-189-88237-232872-17885838&ocompID=119318|title=Player statistics for Luke Schenscher – 2010/11|work=SportsTG.com|accessdate=20 February 2019}} On 23 December, he had 25 points and 10 rebounds against the [[Adelaide 36ers]]. He had another 25-point, 10-rebound effort on 21 January against the Wildcats. In game one of the Crocodiles' semi-final series against the [[Cairns Taipans]], Schenscher recorded 15 points and a season-high 14 rebounds. The Crocodiles went on to lose the series 2–1. In 31 games during the [[2010–11 NBL season|2010–11 season]], he averaged 13.7 points, 6.8 rebounds, 1.4 assists and 1.1 blocks per game. He subsequently earned [[All-NBL Team|All-NBL Second Team]] honours and was named the Club MVP.{{cite web|url=http://www.botinagy.com/blog/big-3-for-next-big-free/|title=Big 3 for next "Big Free"|website=BotiNagy.com|access-date=1 May 2020}} After considering a move back to Adelaide,{{cite web|last=Nagy|first=Boti|url=http://www.adelaidenow.com.au/sport/luke-perth-star-on-36ers-horizon/story-e6frecj3-1226056392355|title=Luke, Perth star on 36ers' horizon|work=AdelaideNow.com.au|date=15 May 2011|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20120808061423/http://www.adelaidenow.com.au/sport/luke-perth-star-on-36ers-horizon/story-e6frecj3-1226056392355|archivedate=8 August 2012}} Schenscher returned to the Crocodiles for the [[2011–12 NBL season|2011–12 season]].
